from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initializing the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Prior: Setting the Stage", 
            [
                'Let this unit square represent all possible outcomes.', 
                'In our forest, ten percent are rare Golden Squirrels.', 
                'This vertical strip shows our initial prior belief.', 
                'The other ninety percent are common Grey Squirrels.', 
                'Area represents probability in this geometric model.'
            ]
        )
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_GREY = "#808080"
        COLOR_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"

        # Constructing the geometric components
        gold_rect = Rectangle(width=0.4, height=4, fill_color=COLOR_GOLD, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        grey_rect = Rectangle(width=3.6, height=4, fill_color=COLOR_GREY, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        strips = VGroup(gold_rect, grey_rect).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0)
        
        square_outline = Square(side_length=4, color=COLOR_WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        divider = Line(UP*2, DOWN*2, color=COLOR_WHITE, stroke_width=2)
        
        # Labels - Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX environment errors
        label_sample = Text("Sample Space", color=COLOR_WHITE, font_size=24)
        label_gold = Text("P(Gold)=0.1", color=COLOR_GOLD, font_size=24)
        label_grey = Text("P(Grey)=0.9", color=COLOR_GREY, font_size=32)

        # Positioning (using area and grid)
        diagram_group = VGroup(strips, square_outline, divider)
        self.place_in_area(diagram_group, "A1", "F6")
        
        # Placing labels relative to the grid
        self.place_at_grid(label_sample, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(label_gold, "B2", scale_factor=0.7) 
        self.place_at_grid(label_grey, "B4", scale_factor=1.0) 

        # Adjust divider line to its 10% position within the square
        divider.move_to(square_outline.get_center() + LEFT * 1.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_WHITE),
            Create(square_outline),
            Write(label_sample)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_GOLD),
            Create(divider),
            FadeIn(gold_rect)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_GOLD),
            Write(label_gold)
        )
        self.play(
            Indicate(gold_rect, color=COLOR_WHITE, scale_factor=1.05),
            Flash(gold_rect, color=COLOR_WHITE, line_length=0.2, flash_radius=0.5),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_GREY),
            FadeIn(grey_rect),
            Write(label_grey)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(COLOR_WHITE),
            label_gold.animate.scale(1.2),
            label_grey.animate.scale(1.1)
        )
        self.play(
            label_gold.animate.scale(1/1.2),
            label_grey.animate.scale(1/1.1)
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title = "The Geometry of New Information"
        lines = [
            'Suppose the camera glints, giving us new evidence.', 
            'We discard all regions where no glint occurred.', 
            'Our universe shrinks to only the shaded areas.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_GREY = "#888888"
        COLOR_DISCARD = "#222222"
        COLOR_OUTLINE = "#FFFFFF"

        # Define the geometric components
        # Gold Strip (Prior for Gold Coin) - Split into Glint (80%) and No Glint (20%)
        # A to E is 5 units, F is 1 unit. Total 6.
        gold_glint = Rectangle(width=3, height=5, fill_color=COLOR_GOLD, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        gold_no_glint = Rectangle(width=3, height=1, fill_color=COLOR_GOLD, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        
        # Grey Strip (Prior for Fair Coin) - Split into Glint (20%) and No Glint (80%)
        # A is 1 unit, B to F is 5 units. Total 6.
        grey_glint = Rectangle(width=3, height=1, fill_color=COLOR_GREY, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        grey_no_glint = Rectangle(width=3, height=5, fill_color=COLOR_GREY, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)

        # Labels to be inherited/simulated from Section 2
        label_gold = Text("Gold", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        label_grey = Text("Grey", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        prob_label_1 = Text("0.8", font_size=18, color=WHITE)
        prob_label_2 = Text("0.2", font_size=18, color=WHITE)

        # Position elements
        self.place_in_area(gold_glint, "A1", "E3")
        self.place_in_area(gold_no_glint, "F1", "F3")
        self.place_in_area(grey_glint, "A4", "A6")
        self.place_in_area(grey_no_glint, "B4", "F6")

        self.place_at_grid(label_gold, "A2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_grey, "A5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_label_1, "C2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(prob_label_2, "D5", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Initial appearance (re-establishing state from Section 2)
        self.add(gold_glint, gold_no_glint, grey_glint, grey_no_glint)
        self.add(label_gold, label_grey, prob_label_1, prob_label_2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Suppose the camera glints, giving us new evidence.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_GOLD),
            gold_glint.animate.set_stroke(COLOR_GOLD, 2),
            grey_glint.animate.set_stroke(COLOR_GREY, 2),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # We discard all regions where no glint occurred.
        # Bottom 20% of gold and bottom 80% of grey turn dark grey.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_GREY),
            gold_no_glint.animate.set_fill(COLOR_DISCARD),
            grey_no_glint.animate.set_fill(COLOR_DISCARD),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Our universe shrinks to only the shaded areas.
        # Bold white outline and fade out labels.
        outline_gold = Rectangle(width=3, height=5, stroke_color=COLOR_OUTLINE, stroke_width=6, fill_opacity=0)
        outline_grey = Rectangle(width=3, height=1, stroke_color=COLOR_OUTLINE, stroke_width=6, fill_opacity=0)
        self.place_in_area(outline_gold, "A1", "E3")
        self.place_in_area(outline_grey, "A4", "A6")

        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_OUTLINE),
            FadeOut(label_gold),
            FadeOut(label_grey),
            FadeOut(prob_label_1),
            FadeOut(prob_label_2),
            Create(outline_gold),
            Create(outline_grey),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Configuration and Directory Setup
        os.makedirs(os.path.join("media", "texts"), exist_ok=True)
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"

        # 1. Title and Layout Initialization
        title_text = "Bayes' Theorem: The Geometry of Logic"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Prior Belief: P(H)",
            "- New Evidence: E",
            "- Likelihood: P(E|H)",
            "- Posterior: P(H|E)"
        ]
        
        self.display_sidebar(title_text, lecture_lines)
        self.visualize_bayes_geometry()
        self.wait(2)

    def display_sidebar(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # Title at the top
        title = Text(title_text, font_size=32, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(title)

        # Left-side sidebar content
        lecture_mobjects = [Text(line, font_size=24, color=GRAY_A) for line in lecture_lines]
        sidebar = VGroup(*lecture_mobjects).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.5)
        sidebar.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(sidebar), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(sidebar[0].animate.set_color(BLUE), sidebar[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

    def visualize_bayes_geometry(self):
        # Container for the visualization area (Right Side)
        viz_center = RIGHT * 3
        
        # Dimensions for probabilities
        sq_width = 5
        sq_height = 4
        prior_p_h = 0.4
        likelihood_e_h = 0.8
        likelihood_e_not_h = 0.2
        
        # Sample Space
        sample_space = Rectangle(width=sq_width, height=sq_height, color=WHITE).move_to(viz_center)
        
        # H and Not H areas
        h_rect = Rectangle(
            width=sq_width * prior_p_h, 
            height=sq_height, 
            fill_color=BLUE, 
            fill_opacity=0.3, 
            stroke_width=1
        ).align_to(sample_space, LEFT).align_to(sample_space, UP)
        
        not_h_rect = Rectangle(
            width=sq_width * (1 - prior_p_h), 
            height=sq_height, 
            fill_color=GRAY_C, 
            fill_opacity=0.1, 
            stroke_width=1
        ).align_to(sample_space, RIGHT).align_to(sample_space, UP)
        
        # Labels for H and Not H - Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency errors
        label_h = Text("H", color=BLUE, font_size=32).next_to(h_rect, UP)
        label_not_h = Text("¬H", color=GRAY_C, font_size=32).next_to(not_h_rect, UP)

        # Evidence areas (Intersection with H and Not H)
        e_intersect_h = Rectangle(
            width=sq_width * prior_p_h,
            height=sq_height * likelihood_e_h,
            fill_color=YELLOW,
            fill_opacity=0.7,
            stroke_width=0
        ).align_to(h_rect, DOWN).align_to(h_rect, LEFT)
        
        e_intersect_not_h = Rectangle(
            width=sq_width * (1 - prior_p_h),
            height=sq_height * likelihood_e_not_h,
            fill_color=YELLOW,
            fill_opacity=0.3,
            stroke_width=0
        ).align_to(not_h_rect, DOWN).align_to(not_h_rect, RIGHT)

        # Animation Sequence
        self.play(Create(sample_space))
        self.play(
            FadeIn(h_rect), FadeIn(not_h_rect),
            Write(label_h), Write(label_not_h)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Showing Evidence E
        e_label = Text("E", color=YELLOW, font_size=32).next_to(e_intersect_h, LEFT)
        self.play(
            FadeIn(e_intersect_h), 
            FadeIn(e_intersect_not_h),
            Write(e_label)
        )
        
        # Highlight Posterior P(H|E) - The part of E that belongs to H
        posterior_box = SurroundingRectangle(e_intersect_h, color=GOLD, buff=0.05)
        # Using Text for formula to ensure compatibility in environments without LaTeX
        posterior_math = Text("P(H|E) = P(E and H) / P(E)", font_size=26).next_to(sample_space, DOWN, buff=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(posterior_box))
        self.play(Write(posterior_math))
        self.wait(1)

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        """
        Sets up the scene layout with a title, left-side lecture notes, 
        and a coordinate grid system for the right-side visualization.
        """
        # Set Background
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        
        # Title Setup
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets)
        lecture_vgroup = VGroup(*[
            Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines
        ]).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        
        self.lecture = lecture_vgroup.scale(0.8).to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7)

        # Define 6x6 animation grid for the right side of the screen
        self.grid_coords = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Centered roughly on the right half: x from 1 to 5, y from 2 to -2
                x_pos = 1.5 + (j * 0.9)
                y_pos = 2.0 - (i * 0.8)
                self.grid_coords[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x_pos, y_pos, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        """Helper to place a mobject at a specific grid coordinate."""
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid_coords[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # 1. Initialize Layout and Content
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Bayes' Theorem Logic",
            "- Geometric Area Updates",
            "- Prior Probability Mapping",
            "- Likelihood Constraints"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout("Bayes' Theorem: The Geometry of Belief", lecture_lines)

        # 2. Create Visualization Objects
        # Representing concepts with basic geometric shapes
        prior_box = Square(side_length=0.8, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        likelihood_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        evidence_tri = Triangle().scale(0.4).set_color(PURPLE).set_fill(PURPLE, opacity=0.3)

        # 3. Position Mobjects using Grid Logic
        self.place_at_grid(prior_box, "A1")
        self.place_at_grid(likelihood_circle, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(evidence_tri, "C3")

        # 4. Animation Sequence
        # Animate Text first
        self.play(
            Write(self.lecture),
            run_time=2.5,
            lag_ratio=0.1
        )
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Animate Geometric Logic
        self.play(
            Create(prior_box),
            FadeIn(prior_box.copy().set_fill(opacity=0.1), scale=1.2),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        self.play(
            Create(likelihood_circle),
            run_time=1
        )

        self.play(
            Create(evidence_tri),
            run_time=1
        )

        # Transition grid objects
        self.play(
            prior_box.animate.move_to(self.grid_coords["D4"]),
            likelihood_circle.animate.move_to(self.grid_coords["E5"]),
            evidence_tri.animate.move_to(self.grid_coords["F6"]),
            run_time=2
        )

        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Bayes' Theorem: The Geometry of Changing Your Mind
outline.target_audience: University students and lifelong learners with a basic grasp of probability

sections.title: The Prior: Setting the Stage
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'Prior Belief' using a unit square (Area = 1) to represent the total sample space. We define the initial probability of an event before seeing any evidence. Visually, this is represented as a vertical slice of the square.
sections.example: Imagine a forest where 10% of the squirrels are 'Golden Squirrels' (rare) and 90% are 'Grey Squirrels'. We represent the Golden Squirrels as a thin vertical strip covering 0.1 of our 1x1 square.

sections.title: The Evidence Filter (Likelihood)
sections.content: Introduce the 'Test' or 'Evidence' (e.g., a sensor or observation). We define the probability of the evidence occurring given the state (Likelihood). Visually, we add a horizontal dimension. We shade the portion of each group (Golden vs. Grey) that would trigger a specific observation (e.g., a 'glint' in the sunlight).
sections.example: A motion-sensor camera 'glints' for 80% of Golden Squirrels (True Positive) but also 'glints' for 20% of Grey Squirrels due to lens flares (False Positive). We shade 80% of the Golden strip and 20% of the Grey strip.

sections.title: The Geometry of New Information
sections.content: This is the 'Conditioning' step. Once we see the evidence (the camera glints), all outcomes that didn't glint become impossible. Visually, we discard (fade out) the unshaded parts of the square. Our 'Universe' has now shrunk to only the shaded regions.
sections.example: The camera flashes! We immediately delete the parts of the square where the camera stayed dark. We are left with two rectangles: a small piece of the 'Golden' territory and a larger-than-expected piece of 'Grey' territory.

sections.title: Normalizing the Space (The Posterior)
sections.content: To find the new probability, we must 're-normalize' our view. We zoom into the remaining shaded areas until they fill a new 1x1 square. The 'Posterior' is the ratio of the 'True Positive' area to the 'Total New Shaded' area.
sections.example: We compare the area of 'Golden-and-Glint' (0.1 * 0.8 = 0.08) against the total glinting area (0.08 + [0.9 * 0.2] = 0.26). Even though the camera glinted, the probability it's a Golden Squirrel is only 0.08 / 0.26 ≈ 30.7%.

sections.title: The Bayesian Formula: From Shapes to Algebra
sections.content: Translate the visual manipulation of areas into the formal Bayes' Theorem formula. Show how the numerator is the overlap area and the denominator is the sum of all 'Evidence-Triggering' areas. Summarize how beliefs change based on the strength of evidence vs. the rarity of the prior.
sections.example: Display the formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Map each variable to the squirrel areas: P(A) is the thin strip, P(B|A) is the height of the glint, and P(B) is the total shaded area.

storyboard.title: The Prior: Setting the Stage
lecture_lines: This unit square represents our entire sample space.
We divide it to represent different possible outcomes.
Ten percent represent rare Golden Squirrels, others are Grey.
These areas show the initial probability of each group.
This gold strip is our prior belief for Golden Squirrels.
animations: Create a unit square (side length 4) with a white outline (#FFFFFF) and label it 'Sample Space' below.
Draw a vertical line at 10% width from the left edge of the square.
Fill the left 10% strip with gold (#FFD700) and the remaining 90% with grey (#808080).
Animate the text labels 'P(Gold)=0.1' and 'P(Grey)=0.9' appearing in the strips.
Apply a pulsing white (#FFFFFF) stroke to the gold strip's border.

storyboard.title: The Evidence Filter (Likelihood)
lecture_lines: A camera glints when detecting a squirrel's presence.
We shade areas where the camera triggers a glint.
These heights represent the likelihood of observing a glint.
animations: Draw a horizontal line at 80% height in the gold strip and 20% height in the grey strip.
Color the top-left area bright yellow (#FFFACD) and the top-right area light grey (#D3D3D3).

Display 'P(Glint|Gold)=0.8' and 'P(Glint|Grey)=0.2' labels near the shaded areas alongside the [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/camera.svg] icon to represent the detection of the glint.

storyboard.title: The Geometry of New Information
lecture_lines: When the camera glints, non-glinting outcomes become impossible.
We focus only on the regions where evidence occurred.
The rest of the sample space is now discarded.
animations: Animate the bottom 20% of the gold strip and bottom 80% of the grey strip turning dark grey (#222222).
Create a bold white (#FFFFFF) outline around the top-left and top-right shaded areas.
Fade out all labels from the previous step, leaving only the shaded rectangles and their new borders.

storyboard.title: Normalizing the Space (The Posterior)
lecture_lines: Let's combine the remaining areas to form a new space.
This total area represents all possible glinting events.
We normalize this space back into a unit square.
The gold region's relative size gives the new probability.
This updated value is called the posterior probability.
animations: Translate the gold-glint and grey-glint rectangles to the center, side-by-side, removing gaps.
Add a white (#FFFFFF) brace at the bottom spanning both rectangles, labeled 'Total Evidence: 0.26'.
Scale the grouped rectangles to occupy a 4x4 area, filling the original square's space.
Show the math text '0.08 / 0.26 ≈ 31%' appearing centered in the now-larger gold section.
Change the label of the gold section to 'Posterior P(Gold|Glint)' in gold text (#FFD700).

storyboard.title: The Bayesian Formula: From Shapes to Algebra
lecture_lines: These geometric steps form the famous Bayes' Theorem formula.
The gold term represents our initial prior belief.
The yellow term is the likelihood from our evidence.
We divide by the total probability of the evidence.
This formula elegantly captures how we update our knowledge.
animations: Transform the visual areas into the text 'P(A|B) = [P(B|A)P(A)] / P(B)' in the center of the screen.
Color the 'P(A)' term gold (#FFD700) to match the initial strip color.
Color the 'P(B|A)' term bright yellow (#FFFACD) to match the likelihood height color.
Color the denominator 'P(B)' white (#FFFFFF) and highlight it with an underline.
Apply a final pulsing glow to the entire formula in white (#FFFFFF).
